non_overlapping_arithmetic.principle: Every source in this category is on ONE lineage rooted at FineMath-3+, except algebraic-stack. Only lineage roots may be summed.
non_overlapping_arithmetic.lineage_tree: finemath-3plus (root, 34.69B measured) -> finemath-4plus (subset, 10.06B measured) -> swallow-math-v2 stage1 length-filter -> stage2 LLM math extraction -> stage3 {qa 14.65B, textbook 19.01B} (both LLM rewrites of the SAME source docs). Separately: infiwebmath-3plus (partly-independent root, unmeasured) -> infiwebmath-4plus (subset). Separately: algebraic-stack (fully independent, math CODE, unmeasured).

meets_3x_peak_demand_detail: 3x peak demand = 21B. The measured non-overlapping total of 34.69B is 4.96x the 7B peak demand, so the 3x floor is met on MEASURED tokens alone, from finemath-3plus by itself.
meets_plan_pool_36B_detail: 34.69B measured vs a 36B plan pool — SHORT by 1.31B (3.6%). Closing it needs exactly one thing: a real count of infiwebmath-3plus (projected 22.02B), which would clear 36B with wide margin even after a large overlap discount. algebraic-stack (10.96B) is a second, license-blocked route.
overlaps: swallow-math-v2 (both configs) is an LLM rewrite of FineMath-3+, stated on its own card ('derived from FineMath-3+', stage1 = 'Filtered subset of finemath-3+ by text length'). Its ~33.7B tokens are the SAME documents as finemath-3plus in new prose. Summing FineMath + SwallowMath double-counts the corpus; the design doc's 'dedupe or substitute' is correct, and SUBSTITUTE is the cleaner call because the rewrite defeats document-level dedup entirely — it is not near-duplicate text, it is regenerated text about the same content.

swallow-math-v2-qa and swallow-math-v2-textbook overlap EACH OTHER, not just FineMath: both are stage-3 rewrites of the same stage-2 extraction in two different styles. They are two views of one corpus. Using both = ~2 epochs of the same documents wearing different clothes.
finemath-4plus is a card-declared subset of finemath-3plus (measured 10.06B of the 34.69B). Same for infiwebmath-4plus within infiwebmath-3plus.

finemath-3plus and infiwebmath-3plus OVERLAP and the FineMath card proves it: curation Phase 2 step 2 'Added URLs from OpenWebMath and InfiMM-WebMath datasets' into the FineMath candidate pool, and results finding 4 says 'Deduplicating the pages repeated between FineMath and InfiWebMath reduces performance compared to a non-deduplicated combination' — an explicit admission of repeated pages. The card's own combined figure is telling: 34B + 20.5B = 54.5B naively, and it advertises 54B, so HF is NOT netting the overlap out either. I attempted to MEASURE this overlap by sampling infiwebmath-3plus URLs and querying /filter on finemath-3plus for each (the /filter endpoint does work on this repo); 114 URLs were sampled before the 429 stop order landed, so the overlap fraction is unquantified. This is a cheap, high-value measurement to finish — it is the difference between a 36B pool and a padded one.

SwallowMath-v2 inherits FineMath's decontamination and nothing more. FineMath removed 13-gram overlaps against GSM8k/MATH/MMLU/ARC test sets, but SwallowMath REWROTE those documents with Qwen3-235B afterwards. Per the project's existing 'rephrased synthetic hides contamination' finding, rephrasing is exactly what defeats n-gram decontam — so SwallowMath-v2's effective decontamination status is WEAKER than its FineMath parent's, not equal to it.

method_notes: 429s degraded even the runs that completed: finemath-4plus landed 135 usable docs at 60 distinct offsets instead of the requested 300, and swallow-math-v2-qa FAILED outright on the second attempt after 5 consecutive 429s (its number here is salvaged from the first attempt's log). Small-n sampling widens the sample-mean CI but does NOT bias the stats-ratio estimator, whose heavy-tailed factor comes from /statistics over the whole split — this is exactly the robustness the factored estimator was built for, and it is why these numbers are still usable.

No dataset bytes were downloaded. All calls were datasets-server metadata endpoints (/size, /splits, /statistics, /rows, /info, /filter) plus the HF repo API (/api/datasets/...) for licenses and file sizes. No load_dataset(), no hf_hub_download of a data file.

Every license was read from cardData AND cross-checked against the card body prose, because the two disagree in the one case that matters: proof-pile-2 has no license field at all and its prose declines to grant one.
